title.narrative: Promoting GBV Response and Prevention for Emergency affected Persons of 21600 (16200 women and 5400 girls) in Kaxda district of Banadir region, Somalia

description.narrative:
ltp style="mso-margin-top-alt:automso-margin-bottom-alt:auto" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtThe proposed project is a complementary and upgrading of an existing of two GBV One stop center (OSC) and one Women and girl’s safe space (WGSS) in Kahda district which hosts the main IDPs in Mogadishu Somalia the centers were funded by UNFPA/FCDO but the funding came to an end March 2023. The centers are the only facility with qualified staff able to offer post rape treatment and psycho social support for the survivors in the targeted location. The Centers are facing funding challenges SCC is now self-supporting continuity of the services but may not secure funding to continue the support of the services for all centers and the need of GBV services is higher due to droughts everyday there are new arrivals at the IDPs in Kahda. The Center is currently run by its staff voluntarily. The planned project is to support the continuity and complementary of services at the established Center that focuses on increased access to integrated friendly services for gender based violence survivors and those at risk through promotion of GBV risk mitigation and provision of comprehensive GBV services. The project targets to reach out to 21600 (16200 women and 5400 girls) in Kaxda IDP camps, new arrivals and poor host communities in kahda, The project will create community engagement on GBV prevention and response services for the survivors. The project will also increase ease access to integrated friendly services for gender based survivors affected by drought and conflicts in (sexual reproductive health, psycho social support, Provision of clinical management of rape services through existing GBV one stop centers and women girl’s safe space and safe shelter, Support for cash and vouchers assistance through case management systems and conditional cash transfers (within the standard GBV criteria) to individual vulnerable women and girls, Dignity kits ,menstrual hygiene kits support and vocational training skills to create a livelihood opportunity for the survivors). The project will also distribute solar lamps to affected IDPs that will contribute in reducing attacks and rape incidents to happen at night due to poor lighting in the IDP camps. The intervention shall include the following activities: Live saving post rape treatment and psychological support for rape survivors. Timely post rape treatment Within 72 hours of the sexual assault and psychological support will be provided to the rape survivors. treatment of injuries, STIs and prevent HIV transmission, pregnancy will be given to survivors, lifesaving material assistance to be provided to emergency affected IDPs and GBV survivors in Kahda, provision of life saving material assistance of dignity kits to IDP women/returnees and GBV survivors. Selection of beneficiaries will be involved with local authorities, community leaders and IDPs, A community outreach team will include to connect IDPs people in need with the right community organizations and resources. The main focus of a main component of mobile outreach work is to provide basic needs, harm- reduction tools, and peer recovery support to vulnerable populations that often have little or no access to services, including people who are living in IDPs and Poor hosting communities to support, assist, and empower vulnerable people. On CMR for GBV survivors, confidential referral pathways/set standards and psycho social services (PSS) and outreach awareness raising through mobile teams to mobilize and provide information for service available in the GBV centers. The mobile team will organize sessions at the sites and villages in kahda.
